title: Branch History Table (2-Bit Counters)
constraints: 16 two-bit saturating counters indexed by `pc[5:2]` (instructions are 4-byte aligned). Reset sets every counter to 01 (weakly not-taken).
Prediction (combinational): `ctr` = the counter for `pc`, and `pred = ctr[1]` (taken when the counter is 2 or 3).
On a rising edge with `update`, the counter for `upd_pc` moves toward the outcome: +1 if `taken` (saturating at 3), −1 if not (saturating at 0).
hints: An array of 2-bit registers, one read port (prediction) and one write port (update).
Saturation: only increment when the counter isn't already 3, and only decrement when it isn't 0.
Why two bits? A loop branch mispredicts only once per loop exit instead of twice (hysteresis).

examples.title: training
examples.input: update the branch at 0x40 as taken 4 times

examples.check: hysteresis: one mispredict does not flip
